title: Egg Omelet with Meat Cooked with Cooking Spray

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet with meat prepared using cooking spray is a quick dish that became popular in the early 1990s. Eggs are beaten, pieces of cooked pork are added, and the mixture is cooked in a pan sprayed with a non‑fat cooking spray, reducing added fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish emerged in the United States in the early 1990s when cooking sprays entered the mass market.
The spray allows cooking without oil while preserving the flavor and texture of the meat.
The omelet is often served with toast, fresh vegetables, or mashed potatoes.
Variations include cheese, herbs, onions, or bell peppers.
Its fast preparation makes it popular among students and busy professionals.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs and pork provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and overall tissue maintenance.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Both eggs and meat supply B12, B6, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Low added fat
items.content: Using cooking spray instead of oil reduces the amount of saturated fat in the dish.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Pork contributes iron and zinc, important for immune function and blood formation.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and a small amount of fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium in spray
items.content: Cooking sprays often contain salt; people monitoring sodium intake should use them sparingly.

items.title: Meat quality
items.content: Use fresh or properly stored pork to avoid the risk of foodborne illness.

items.title: Egg freshness
items.content: Eggs should be fresh; older eggs can harbor salmonella.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; individuals with high cholesterol should limit consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the omelet hot, cut into portions. It pairs well with whole‑grain toast, fresh vegetables, avocado, or a light sauce. Optional toppings include grated cheese, herbs, or hot sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The omelet is best eaten immediately. If needed, store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat in a dry pan or microwave to retain texture.
